items.title: Indian teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits record 204 off 53 balls
items.why: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, 15, scored 204 off 53 balls for India A against the UAE in Doha on Tuesday, setting 50-over (List A) records for the fastest hundred (28 balls) and double hundred (52 balls). He also hit a record 28 sixes as India won by seven wickets.

items.title: Israeli strikes in Gaza kill senior Hamas security official and six others
items.why: Israeli strikes in Gaza on Tuesday killed at least seven people, including Naeem Abu Nahel, head of Hamas's internal security service, according to Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry and medics. Israel's military said it struck a senior militant. The strikes came despite the ceasefire agreed in October 2025.

items.title: Pakistani astronaut set to be first foreigner aboard China's space station
items.why: Pakistan Air Force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, 40, is due to launch on China's Shenzhou-24 mission from Jiuquan at 00:18 GMT on Wednesday. He would be the first Pakistani in space and the first foreign astronaut on the Tiangong station, where he will spend about a week.
items.matters: It is China's first crewed space mission to include an astronaut from another country.

items.title: Iraq orders federal takeover of oilfields in Kurdish-controlled areas
items.why: Iraq's prime minister, Ali al-Zaidi, on Tuesday ordered the federal Oil Ministry to run oilfields under Kurdish security control in Kirkuk, Nineveh, Diyala and Salahuddin, and federal authorities to take over the Kurdish region's border crossings. Kurdish Prime Minister Masrour Barzani called the orders unacceptable.
items.matters: Control of oil and its income has long divided Baghdad and the Kurdish region; this could deepen the dispute.

items.title: Pope Francis's private diary, now published, describes seeing the devil
items.why: A book of the late Pope Francis's private notes from 1992 to 2024, edited by Cardinal Víctor Manuel Fernández, came out on Tuesday in five languages. In it Francis describes seeing the devil several times and a spiritual crisis in 2021 and 2022.

items.title: Solomon Islands to end security pact with China, reports say
items.why: Solomon Islands has told China it will not renew their 2022 security pact when it expires in April 2027, ABC Australia and Reuters report, citing unnamed sources. Prime Minister Matthew Wale is in Canberra to sign a new treaty with Australia on Wednesday.
items.matters: The 2022 pact alarmed Australia and the US because it opened the way for Chinese forces in the South Pacific.

items.title: Bangladesh's ousted leader Sheikh Hasina says she will return on 16 December
items.why: Sheikh Hasina, Bangladesh's former prime minister, plans to return from exile in India on 16 December, her spokesman says, and has asked for a flight on the state airline. She was sentenced to death in her absence. A government minister says she can only return in handcuffs.

items.title: California braces for flooding as king tides meet strong El Niño
items.why: Exceptionally high 'king tides' peaking on Wednesday, a strong El Niño and record-warm seas could bring severe coastal flooding to California during Thanksgiving week, AFP reports. The US National Weather Service warns of up to nearly three feet (0.9m) of flooding around San Francisco Bay.
items.matters: San Francisco's mayor, Daniel Lurie, has urged people to limit unnecessary travel in the busiest US travel week.

items.title: Australia moves to fine tech giants up to 5% of global revenue
items.why: Australia's Labor government struck a deal with the Greens on Tuesday to pass its digital duty of care bill. Platforms failing to protect users could be fined up to 5% of global revenue, up from a proposed A$109 million; Australians could sue them. The opposition Coalition opposes it.
items.matters: SBS estimates Meta alone could face fines of around A$10 billion; the US ambassador has objected to the law.

items.title: South Korea protests after Russian warplanes fly close to its airspace
items.why: Fewer than five Russian military aircraft entered South Korea's air defence zone near Ulleung Island early on Tuesday, then turned away as fighter jets were scrambled, the military says. A brief emergency alert wrongly called them North Korean. Seoul summoned Russia's defence attaché to protest.
items.matters: It was the third such Russian flight in eight days, the Korea Herald reports.

items.title: Mexico will try captured cartel suspect 'El Chapo Isidro' at home
items.why: Mexico's attorney general, Ernestina Godoy, said on Monday that Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, one of the FBI's ten most wanted fugitives, will be tried in Mexico despite a US extradition request. He was captured in Guasave, Sinaloa, in a raid in which officials say 20 people died.
items.matters: Mexican officials say a US surveillance drone, flown with Mexico's permission, helped track him.

items.title: UN chief calls for global AI safety framework within a year
items.why: Closing a UN summit on AI safety in Bridgetown, Barbados, on Monday, Secretary-General António Guterres urged countries to agree within a year on a shared framework for managing AI risks, with common testing and independent oversight. He leaves office at the end of December.
items.matters: Guterres warns that control over AI is concentrating in a few companies and two countries.

items.title: Quebec court says lawmakers must swear oath to King Charles
items.why: Judge Ian Demers of Quebec's Superior Court on Monday suspended a 2022 law that let members of the Canadian province's National Assembly skip the oath to the British monarch. Premier Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, who calls the oath 'humiliating', says his government will appeal.
items.matters: The ruling could delay the new legislature, due to open on 1 December after October's election.

items.title: Pennsylvania confirms ninth measles death as US outbreak grows
items.why: Pennsylvania's health department confirmed on Monday that a resident of Centre County, who Al Jazeera says was unvaccinated, had died: the state's ninth measles-related death this year. The state has recorded 1,638 cases in 46 counties. Nationally, 5,838 cases were confirmed by 19 November, the most since 1991.
items.matters: The US recently lost the measles-free status it had held for more than 25 years.

items.title: Two US states sue Musk's SpaceX over sexual images made by Grok
items.why: Virginia and Oregon filed separate consumer-protection lawsuits on Monday against SpaceX, X and other Musk companies. They say the Grok AI chatbot's 'spicy mode' was used to make sexual images of real people, including children, without proper safeguards. X says users who did this broke its rules.
items.matters: They are the first US states to sue over Grok's images; they want damages, penalties and court orders.

items.title: UK to host 2035 Women's World Cup; US-led bid gets 2031
items.why: FIFA's member associations approved both unopposed bids by acclamation at a virtual meeting on Monday. England, Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland will host in 2035. The United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica will host in 2031, the first edition with 48 teams.
items.matters: It will be the first World Cup played in the UK since the men's tournament in England in 1966.

items.title: Bangladesh garment workers reject factory owners' pay offer
items.why: Talks at Bangladesh's garment wage board in Dhaka ended on Monday without agreement after workers' representatives rejected the owners' undisclosed offer. Workers want a monthly minimum of 32,000 taka (about $258), up from 12,500 taka. Talks resume on Tuesday afternoon.
items.matters: Strikes have closed about 500 factories in an industry that employs about four million people, Al Jazeera reports.

items.title: EU proposes banning Russian teams from sport in new sanctions package
items.why: The European Commission proposed its 22nd package of sanctions on Russia on Monday. It would bar Russian teams and athletes from competing under Russia's flag at EU events, restrict 60 Russian banks and ban entry to Russians who fought in Ukraine. All 27 EU countries must agree.
items.matters: Ursula von der Leyen says the EU will keep proposing sanctions until Russia shows genuine intent for lasting peace.

items.title: Hacker who leaked Grand Theft Auto VI clips sentenced to seven years
items.why: Arion Kurtaj, 21, was sentenced at Woolwich Crown Court in London on Monday for hacking Rockstar Games, BT/EE, Revolut and Uber in 2021 and 2022. He leaked 90 clips of the unreleased game. He walked free because of the time he had already spent in custody.

items.title: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang as chief after Trump intervention
items.why: Nvidia's board reinstated co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive on Monday, 11 days after he resigned over affairs, including one with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China. China denies she is a spy. President Trump says he helped convince the board.
items.matters: Democrats and some Republicans want investigations; Huang faces questions from House committees on 1 December and a Senate committee on 3 December.

items.title: Lego to build €1bn factory in Portugal, its eighth worldwide
items.why: Danish toymaker Lego will build a factory in Estarreja, near Aveiro in northern Portugal, investing about €1bn and creating more than 1,000 jobs, it announced on Monday. Construction starts in 2027 and brick production in 2030. It will be Lego's fourth factory in Europe.

items.title: Iran flogs singer Parastoo Ahmadi over concert without headscarf
items.why: Singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four members of her team were each given 74 lashes in Qom on Monday, her lawyer Mostafa Nili told Iranian media. A court convicted them over a 2024 online concert in which she sang without a hijab. Rights groups call flogging torture.
items.matters: They also face two-year bans on performing and on leaving Iran.

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy rival Zscaler for $43.9bn
items.why: US cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike will buy Zscaler in an all-share deal valuing it at about $43.9bn, the companies said on Monday. Zscaler shareholders get a 34% premium. The deal needs shareholder and regulatory approval and is expected to close in CrowdStrike's 2028 financial year.
items.matters: Euronews calls it the biggest cybersecurity deal ever, combining two firms that protect many large organisations.

items.title: India pledges $1.6bn to help flood-hit Nepal rebuild
items.why: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced a 240 billion Nepali rupee (about $1.6bn) package in New Delhi on Monday during a visit by Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah. Nepal's August glacier flood killed about 1,500 people, and 5,200 are missing, Reuters reports.
items.matters: Nepal puts rebuilding costs at about three times India's offer, so it still needs much more help.

items.title: Belgian airports halt flights as unions strike against government cuts
items.why: Air traffic controllers joined a national day of union action on Monday, halting flights at Brussels and Charleroi airports from 07:00 to 21:00 local time. About 59,500 passengers had been booked on 429 Brussels flights. Unions oppose Prime Minister Bart De Wever's austerity budget.
items.matters: Airlines say it is the 11th strike affecting Belgian airspace in 11 months.

items.title: Astronomers say an Earth-sized planet may be hiding beyond Neptune
items.why: Simulations by astronomers in Japan, Australia and the US suggest a planet of 1.5 to 2 times Earth's mass could orbit at 350 to 500 times Earth's distance from the Sun, explaining the odd orbits of distant icy objects. The study is in Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society.
items.matters: Nobody has seen it yet; the new Vera C. Rubin Observatory in Chile may be able to confirm or rule it out.

items.title: Three Salvadoran soldiers killed in Haiti blast, Bukele says
items.why: El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele says three soldiers died in Haiti on Friday when a grenade they were trying to remove from a drone exploded. They were among about 2,500 Salvadoran troops sent to fight gangs after four Salvadorans went missing in an attack on 18 October.
items.matters: Bukele says any soldier who wants to leave Haiti can do so without reprisal.

items.title: Molly Meldrum, Australian music presenter and Countdown host, dies at 83
items.why: Ian 'Molly' Meldrum died in hospital in Melbourne on Monday morning after a period of declining health, his management said. He hosted ABC TV's music show Countdown from 1974 to 1987, helping to launch Australian acts and bring stars such as ABBA and Madonna to Australian audiences.
items.matters: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and many musicians paid tribute to a figure who shaped Australian pop for decades.

items.changed: Updated: Wall Street rebounded after Nvidia reinstated its chief executive
items.title: Wall Street rebounds sharply as Nvidia shares jump 31%
items.why: US stocks surged on Monday after Nvidia reinstated its chief executive. The S&P 500 rose 4.7% and the Nasdaq 6.5%, AP reports, after Friday's AI-driven sell-off. Nvidia shares rose 31.5%, adding about $950bn in value, which NBC News calls the biggest one-day gain in market history.
items.matters: Many people's savings and pensions are invested in the big tech firms that drive these markets.

items.title: Thailand's Jeeno Thitikul wins LPGA Tour Championship for third year running
items.why: Jeeno Thitikul shot a bogey-free 65 to win the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship in Naples, Florida, on Sunday by two shots from Japan's Aki Iwai. The $4m prize, the biggest in women's golf, made her the LPGA's all-time top earner.
items.matters: She passed Annika Sörenstam's career prize-money record, which had stood for 25 years.

items.title: Democrats win largest US House majority since 1992 after recount
items.why: Democrat Chuck Hubbard won North Carolina's 5th district after a recount, beating long-serving Republican Virginia Foxx by about 330 votes. That gives Democrats at least 258 of the 435 House seats in the November midterms, their most since 1992. Four races are still undecided.
items.matters: A large majority lets Democrats control the House agenda and investigations for the second half of President Trump's term.

items.title: Fighting near Congo hospital traps health workers in Ebola outbreak zone
items.why: Health workers sheltered in a hospital maternity ward for more than 24 hours as fighting took place nearby in Ituri province, eastern DR Congo, WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said on Sunday. The WHO counts 11,613 confirmed cases and 5,678 deaths in the outbreak by 17 November.
items.matters: It is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak recorded in the country, and violence is making it harder to contain.

items.title: Ukraine says its sea drones hit a Russian warship in Libya
items.why: President Zelensky says Ukrainian sea drones struck the Russian corvette Merkury and a cargo ship off Benghazi in eastern Libya on Sunday, and that the corvette sank. Libyan officials say it was badly damaged and at least 10 people were wounded. Russia has not commented.
items.matters: It shows the war reaching far beyond Ukraine; the UN mission in Libya has called for an independent investigation.

items.title: Alcaraz beats Zverev to win his first ATP Finals title
items.why: Spain's Carlos Alcaraz beat world number one Alexander Zverev of Germany 6-2, 7-6 in the ATP Finals final in Turin, Italy, on Sunday. He saved three set points in the tie-break and won all five of his matches. It is his 30th career title.
items.matters: He joins Agassi, Federer and Djokovic as the only men to win all four majors and the season-ending finals.

items.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties end unity talks without a deal
items.why: Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party held more than four hours of coalition talks in Herzliya, Israel, on Sunday without agreement, and say they will meet again. They disagree over who would lead and over including far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir.
items.matters: Eisenkot has until 6 December, with a possible two-week extension, to form a government after October's election.

items.title: Liverpool beat ten-man Manchester United 4-0 in Pochettino's first game
items.why: Liverpool beat Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield on Sunday in Mauricio Pochettino's first match as United manager. Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. Dominik Szoboszlai, Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz scored. United are 19th in the Premier League.

items.title: Poland says Russia twice plotted to kill Ukrainian-American rapper
items.why: Poland's foreign ministry says Russian intelligence tried to kill the rapper Kyivstoner in Poland in August, where a Russian citizen was detained. Denmark says it foiled a second plot at a concert near Copenhagen in September, charging two men and expelling a Russian diplomat. Russia calls the claims unsubstantiated.

items.changed: Updated: governments and Pacific nations react to the collapse
items.title: COP31 climate talks in Türkiye end without a deal over fossil fuels
items.why: The UN climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ended on Sunday, two days late, without an agreed final text. Oil-producing states blocked any mention of moving away from fossil fuels, so the EU and others rejected it. UN chief António Guterres expressed 'profound frustration'.
items.matters: Al Jazeera says it is the first UN climate summit since Copenhagen in 2009 to end without a deal adopted by all.

items.title: New Hunger Games prequel opens with $225m worldwide box office
items.why: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping took an estimated $120m in North America and $105m in 84 other markets in its opening weekend, studio estimates show. It was the top film in the US despite competition from the launch of the video game Grand Theft Auto VI.

items.title: Istanbul officials say animal in lion hunt was not a big cat
items.why: Teams with drones and thermal cameras searched woods in Uskumruköy, on Istanbul's northern edge, after a resident reported a lion on Sunday evening. On Monday evening the governor's office said new footage showed the animal was 'neither a lion nor any other big cat'. What it was remains unclear.
items.matters: Prosecutors are investigating whether the animal had an owner.
items.changed: Updated: officials now say the animal was not a lion

items.title: Indonesia factory fire: 24 body bags recovered and dozens still missing
items.why: Rescuers had recovered 24 body bags from a burned sweets factory in Cikande, Banten province, west of Jakarta, by Sunday evening, officials say. Remains must be identified by DNA, which could take weeks. About 30 to 34 people are still missing, according to differing official counts.
items.changed: Updated: 24 body bags recovered; about 30 to 34 people still missing

items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers hit mines near Hormuz
items.why: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Monday that three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, two of them under US escort. The claim could not be independently verified, and the US military had not responded. Iran had vowed to counter the US naval blockade.
items.matters: The strait carries a large share of the world's oil, so attacks there affect energy prices everywhere.
items.changed: Updated: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three tankers hit mines in the strait
